citations.source: rocminfo, triton.backends and the DTK toolchain inside the container
citations.locator: Vendor is hygon, not amd: rocminfo reports Vendor Name C-3000 and Device Type HCU where an AMD agent reports AMD and GPU; Triton registers a separate hcu backend with its own HCUDriver beside the amd one and selects it here; the FP16 tl.dot lowers to v_mmac_f32_16x16x16_f16 and to no v_mfma instruction; the hcu backend options carry enable_v_mmac_cluster, mmac_layout_force and hcu_use_gfx946_sched_model_v2; dcc 25.10.0's llc names gfx926, gfx928, gfx936 and gfx938 alongside the AMD CPUs; and the host installs hy-smi and rocm-smi and no amd-smi. The emitted object still carries the amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-- triple, which is the ABI this code object conforms to rather than a statement about the hardware's vendor; observed 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-15 on bw1100

tl.dot emits this ISA's own matrix instruction, spelled v_mmac and not AMD's v_mfma: fp16 operands compile to v_mmac_f32_16x16x16_f16 (16 occurrences) and fp8e4m3 operands to v_mmac_f32_16x16x32_fp8_fp8 (8) beside v_cvt_pk_fp8_f32 (32). The fp8 form's K is 32 against fp16's 16, so the operands reach the matrix unit as fp8 rather than being widened first. An llvm-mc probe using AMD's v_mfma spellings rejected every form including fp16, which is what a shared rule reading how a mnemonic is spelled looks like when it is wrong; observed 2026-09-17 on bw1100

citations.source: triton 3.6.0 tl.dot against a torch fp32 oracle at the same reduced input precision, on BW1101
citations.locator: 64x64x64: fp16 max_abs_error 1.14441e-05 (relative 3.457e-07), fp8e4m3 max_abs_error 0, 0 of 4096 elements outside tolerance and all finite in both. Compilation alone would not license this declaration -- the wave64 shuffle defect (F-2026-09-16-008) compiled and returned wrong numbers -- so the contraction was run and checked elementwise; observed 2026-09-17 on bw1100

citations.source: triton 3.6.0 tl.extra.libdevice.tanh against torch.tanh, on BW1101
citations.locator: Triton's libdevice.tanh lowers to __ocml_tanh_f32 on this target -- AMD's own math library, not CUDA's libdevice, which is why the contract is spelled for ocml -- over v_exp_f32_e32. 1024 inputs spanning [-20, 20] plus a normal sample so the saturating tails are covered: max_abs_error 5.96046e-08, max relative error 1.071e-07, all finite. A composed (e^2x-1)/(e^2x+1) control on the same inputs is 2.181e-06 relative, twenty times worse, which is what distinguishes the library call from a fallback that merely compiles; observed 2026-09-17 on bw1100

citations.source: triton 3.6.0 tl.dot with fp32 operands against torch matmul, on BW1101
citations.locator: fp32 operands reach this ISA's matrix unit rather than falling back to v_fma: input_precision=ieee emits v_mmac_16x16x8_f32 and input_precision=tf32 emits v_mmac_f32_16x16x8_tf32, with zero v_fma or v_pk_fma_f32 in either. 64x64x64 against a torch fp32 matmul: ieee max_abs_error 0 exactly, tf32 relative error 7.177e-04, which is the reduced mantissa and is why the two are separate contracts rather than one. Checked because a contract naming a matrix instruction the hardware does not run for this dtype would be worse than none (F-2026-09-17-011); observed 2026-09-18 on bw1100
